children.title: cjdns
children.description: An encrypted IPv6 network using public-key cryptography for address allocation and a distributed hash table for routing. Source Code

children.title: babled
children.description: Babel is a loop-avoiding distance-vector routing protocol for IPv6 and IPv4 with fast convergence properties. It is based on the ideas in DSDV, AODV and Cisco's EIGRP, but is designed to work well not only in wired networks but also in wireless mesh networks, and has been extended with support for overlay networks. Source Code

children.title: OLSR
children.description: The Optimized Link State Routing Protocol (OLSR) is an IP routing protocol optimized for mobile ad hoc networks, which can also be used on other wireless ad hoc networks. Source Code

children.title: FruityMesh
children.description: The first completely connection-based open source mesh on top of Bluetooth Low Energy 4.1. Source Code

children.title: Mesh Bee
children.description: MeshBee® is a 2.4 GHz wireless zigbee RF module. It use microchip JN516x from NXP that enables several different flavors of standards-based zigbee mesh networking. Source Code

children.title: BLEMP
children.description: Bluetooth Low Energy Mesh Protocol for nRF51 Nordic chips. Source Code

children.title: ZeroNet
children.description: ZeroNet is a decentralized Internet-like network of peer-to-peer users. Each visitor is also a host. Source Code

children.title: Go-IPFS
children.description: IPFS is a global, versioned, peer-to-peer filesystem. It combines good ideas from Git, BitTorrent, Kademlia, SFS, and the Web. It is like a single bittorrent swarm, exchanging git objects. Source Code

children.title: FreeNet
children.description: Communications by Freenet nodes are encrypted and are routed through other nodes to make it extremely difficult to determine who is requesting the information and what its content is, data is shared by all users on the network. Source Code

children.title: Project Byzantium
children.description: Ad-hoc wireless mesh networking for the zombie apocalypse. Unlike most mesh implementations, a Byzantium Mesh requires no specialized equipment that may not be easy to get during an emergency, just an x86 computer with at least one 802.11 a/b/g/n wireless interface. Source Code

children.title: Disaster.radio
children.description: A disaster-resilient communications network powered by the sun. Source Code

children.title: AirChat
children.description: Free Communications For Everyone. Each node only cares for what is being received. No hardware identification, no transmitter plain identification. only packets matter. transmissions are anonymous. whenever an address is needed to reply to a packet, it is encrypted inside the packet. Source Code

children.description: A serverless, unblockable messaging system for Android. Source Code ?

children.title: ServalMesh Batphone
children.description: This app assumes zero infrastructure. The phones talk to each other using WiFi; relaying calls and messages and figuring out how to resolve numbers. In other words, it lets your phone communicate with other Android phones running Serval Mesh within WiFi range. Source Code

children.title: Underdark
children.description: Mobile peer-to-peer mesh networking library. Integrates into iOS and Android apps and works over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Demo app called Solidarity available for download. Source Code (With Extra Clause)
